'''Robert Street''' [[Officer of the Order of Australia|AO]] [[Fellow of the Australian Academy of Science|FAA]] (16 December 1920 &ndash; 4 July 2013) was a British academic and academic administrator.

Born in [[Wakefield]], [[Yorkshire]] and educated at [[Hanley High School, Stoke-on-Trent|Hanley High School]], he was offered a scholarship to [[New College, Oxford]] in 1939, but upon failing to meet the university's [[Latin]] requirement he instead took up a place at [[King's College London]] where he studied physics.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.timeshighereducation.co.uk/news/people/robert-street-1920-2013/2006616.article|title = Robert Street, 1920-2013|date = 22 August 2013}}</ref> He later completed his PhD at [[University of Nottingham|University College, Nottingham]]. He worked as a senior lecturer at the [[University of Sheffield]] from 1954 to 1960 and as Foundation Professor of Physics at [[Monash University]] from 1960 to 1974. He later served as vice-chancellor of the [[University of Western Australia]] from 1978 to 1986.<ref>'STREET, Prof. Robert', Who's Who 2014, A & C Black, an imprint of Bloomsbury Publishing plc, 2014; online edn, Oxford University Press, Dec 2013</ref> He also served as president of the [[Australian Institute of Physics]].<ref name=eoas>[http://www.eoas.info/biogs/P000804b.htm Street, Robert (1920 - 2013)], www.eoas.info</ref>

Street was appointed an [[Officer of the Order of Australia]] in 1985 "For Service to Learning",<ref>{{Cite web |title=Australian Honours Search Facility |url=https://honours.pmc.gov.au/honours/awards/881326 |access-date=2026-01-28 |website=honours.pmc.gov.au}}</ref> was elected a [[Fellow of the Australian Academy of Science]] in 1973<ref name=eoas/> and was awarded the [[Centenary Medal]] in 2001 "For service to Australian society and science in physics".<ref>{{Cite web |title=Australian Honours Search Facility |url=https://honours.pmc.gov.au/honours/awards/1123261 |access-date=2026-01-28 |website=honours.pmc.gov.au}}</ref>
